user_questions.question: Q1 Scope: which payment method data is PII? (A) the Payment_Methods__c object (card number, expiry, card type, brand, default flag) - recommended; (B) A plus the Payment_Method__c picklists on Refund__c and Transaction__c. Q2 Encryption: the org has no Shield tenant secret and the license cannot be confirmed. (A) Shield Platform Encryption (needs license + tenant secret); (B) classic encryption for text fields only, no license - recommended if Shield is not licensed. Q3 Other access: the Data Cloud connector, Slack integration and DMS managed permission sets plus admin profiles have View All Data on the object and cannot be edited. (A) keep them and document - recommended; (B) remove their assignments.
user_questions.simulated_answer: Q1: The Payment_Methods__c object. Payment Methods should be OWD Private, with access only through a finance permission set. Q2: Shield Platform Encryption on the sensitive fields. Q3: No preference; use your recommended default.

skill_friction: AskCoworker was wrong more than twice (missed Payment_Methods__c entirely, wrong picklist values, wrong CRUD, wrong Shield/View Encrypted Data platform claim, wrong profile FLS); the 'two wrong claims' rule triggers early and the skill gives no guidance on whether to re-send D1 with the corrected object set versus proceeding straight to D2.

The user's OWD Private choice requires converting a master-detail to a lookup (changing delete from cascade to restrict); SKILL.md does not say whether a structural consequence of a user decision that changes behavior for other users (Contact deletion) needs a second question, so it was decided as an assumption.

Shield encryptable-field-type support (picklist, checkbox) cannot be tested by any allowed query; the skill says to state documented behavior, but the claim drives which fields are encrypted and could only be handed to a sandbox check.

Residual access through managed, non-editable integration permission sets with View All Data makes 'only the finance team' undeliverable by metadata; the rules do not say whether this is blocking (marked non-blocking with Setup unassignment option).
